transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Brooks (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood PM); Marcus Li (Orion VP Eng), Aisha Khan (Orion Cloud Architect), Noah Green (Orion Procurement)
Links shared: drive.redwood.com/marketplace/packaging-checklist-v1.pdf, git.redwood.com/examples/orion-helm, http://redwood-benchmarks/smoke-run-templates

Summary: quick ops-level sync to align on marketplace packaging, reference-arch validation, billing hooks, and an initial ops runbook for Orion Edge's Azure listing. Action items and dates captured, next joint deploy planned week of 2026-03-23.

Topics: marketplace packaging checklist; Helm/ARM artifacts; container image registry & tagging; SSO/KMS requirements; telemetry and observability hooks; billing/invoicing integration; compliance artifacts for SOC2

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate the time. Quick intro, I'm Lena on the Redwood partnerships team, Diego's our SE who will drive the validation work, Priya on product. Marcus, Aisha, Noah, great to see you.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Hey Lena, thanks. We have about 45 minutes — want to focus on the ops steps to get Orion on the Azure marketplace and how Redwood integrates into our CI/CD.
[00:26] Lena Brooks: Perfect, yeah that's the aim. Diego, do you want to run through the checklist high-level and then dig into any gaps?
[00:33] Diego Ramos: Sure. I'll do a quick run — apologies if I ramble, but I'll try to be concise. First, packaging: we support both ARM templates and Helm charts for marketplace qualification. For our joint listing we prefer Helm because it maps to our internal k8s deployment patterns, but ARM is fine for native Azure offers.
[00:52] Aisha Khan: Quick question — Helm chart, like a single chart with subcharts, or do you want an umbrella? Our infra team usually does umbrella charts.
[01:02] Diego Ramos: Umbrella is ok, but we ask for a top-level values file that sets resource sizing, GPU sku, and quantization/instance flags. Also include a sample values-prod.yaml for marketplace validation — sometimes the automated checks read defaults and they fail if sizes are tiny.
[01:18] Marcus Li: Got it. And about images — do we push to our own registry or Redwood's test registry?
[01:23] Lena Brooks: Short answer: push to your registry and grant Redwood pull access for the validation run. For final listing we provide a recommended public container manifest pattern but you can use your registry behind a service principal.
[01:36] Aisha Khan: Ok, we'll create a service principal. Any particular permission scope?
[01:40] Diego Ramos: Pull-only auth is fine, but for the smoke deployment we need a service principal that can also create role assignments if the chart provisions managed identities. We'll note specifics in the checklist.
[01:50] Noah Green: From procurement side, we need to understand the billing hooks — how does marketplace billing map to Redwood's usage-based pricing, any metering integrations?
[01:59] Priya Nair: I'll jump in — Redwood has two patterns. Marketplace metered billing can be handled via the marketplace metering calls; alternatively, Orion can buy committed capacity and we do reconciliation. For the initial listing we recommend metered usage for flexibility. We'll attach example webhook payloads in the checklist.
[02:18] Marcus Li: Are there any blockers around data residency — Orion needs logs and telemetry to stay in our tenant for 90 days, SOC2 stuff.
[02:25] Diego Ramos: We support private telemetry forwarding. For Redwood Dedicated / Private we can ensure logs don't leave the tenant. For hosted marketplace it depends on the offer type; we'll note the difference and recommended offer type for Orion.
[02:40] Aisha Khan: So if we go with marketplace SaaS — logs might be in Redwood's analytics by default?
[02:45] Lena Brooks: Yeah, typical hosted does central telemetry. If data residency is a must, the marketplace listing can be for a private offer backed by a dedicated deployment or bring-your-own infra where you control the VPC. That's more work but it's supported.
[03:02] Marcus Li: Okay. Let's talk about the reference architecture diagram — Diego, you mentioned a pattern in the docs. Can you summarize required components?
[03:09] Diego Ramos: Sure. Components: Orion k8s cluster, ingress (we recommend nginx or managed app gw), a Redwood inference sidecar or dedicated pod group depending on load, a KV cache layer (note: sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" in automated notes), object storage for model artifacts, service principal for image pulls, and monitoring via Prometheus + Grafana. We also wire up distributed tracing to our tracing endpoint for request IDs.
[03:34] Aisha Khan: For model artifacts, does Redwood expect a certain layout in blob storage?
[03:38] Diego Ramos: Yes, a predictable path: /models/{model-name}/{version}/manifest.json. We'll include a sample manifest in the git repo link. Make sure manifests include tokenization config and quantization flags — those often cause runtime mismatches.
[03:52] Marcus Li: Runtime mismatches — are those common? We had one where the KV cache grew unexpectedly and caused OOMs. Any guidance?
[03:59] Diego Ramos: Yep — ensure your node pools have physics memory headroom and we recommend enabling auto-evict policy for KV cache. Also the Redwood runtime supports shard-aware cache trimming, but that requires a slight config change in values.yaml. We'll include the exact toggles.
[04:18] Noah Green: Back to procurement — what's the timeline for certification? We need to coordinate internal procurement windows.
[04:24] Lena Brooks: Typical marketplace validation + ops run takes 2–3 weeks after we get the artifacts and the test subscription. If you prioritize, we can compress to 1 week but it'd be a focused sprint.
[04:36] Marcus Li: Let's aim for the one-week fast lane if we can get credentials early.
[04:40] Aisha Khan: We'll try. One more thing — SSO: Orion uses SAML SSO and Azure AD. Any special integration?
[04:47] Priya Nair: We support SAML and OIDC. For marketplace single-tenant listings, customers can use their own Azure AD; for multi-tenant SaaS offers, we have a tenant provisioning flow. We'll capture the SAML metadata exchange steps in the checklist.
[05:02] Marcus Li: Sounds good. A quick note on observability — we want our own logs sent to our log ingestion; can we forward raw logs?
[05:09] Diego Ramos: Yes, we can configure a forwarding connector. For Private deployments you own the logs; hosted we forward via secure gated connectors and you can opt out of certain payloads.
[05:23] Aisha Khan: Any gotchas with the marketplace compliance docs — e.g., cert names or expected SOC2 artifacts?
[05:29] Lena Brooks: We'll attach our SOC2 summary and the checklist will list the docs Azure tends to request: data flow diagrams, encryption at rest proof (KMS), and signed SLAs. For private offers, extra attestation is sometimes required.
[05:43] Noah Green: Great. For the joint solution page copy — who owns the marketing assets?
[05:48] Lena Brooks: Redwood can draft the joint listing copy and tech bullets; Orion will review for messaging and compliance. Priya will own the first draft.
[05:56] Priya Nair: I'll draft the tech copy and send a Google Doc link.
[06:00] Marcus Li: Ok — last operational question: what does success look like for the pilot?
[06:06] Diego Ramos: For the ops validation: successful helm deploy in your sandbox, a smoke-run that generates 1k inference tokens with <150ms p50 latency for our small SKU, and successful billing metering events recorded. If all that passes we greenlight marketplace submission.
[06:25] Marcus Li: That's clear.
[06:27] Aisha Khan: Quick FYI — our infra team is on a rotation, so we might have slightly delayed responses next week but we'll prioritize the service principal.
[06:36] Lena Brooks: Understood. We'll send the checklist today. Diego, you'll lead the validation?
[06:40] Diego Ramos: Yes, I'll own validation and coordinate with Aisha. I'll also post the helm template to the git repo and the CI job that runs the smoke tests.
[06:49] Noah Green: And procurement — I'll confirm PO timeline and get an estimate from finance.
[06:54] Lena Brooks: Perfect. Recap: Lena to share checklist + billing notes; Diego to push Helm + validation script; Aisha to set up sandbox and SP; Noah to confirm procurement timeline; Priya to draft listing copy. We'll tentatively schedule the joint deploy for week of 2026-03-23.
[07:12] Marcus Li: Thanks, everyone. That was efficient.
[07:16] Lena Brooks: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.
[07:20] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: automated transcript contained occasional word swaps (e.g., "KV" vs "K V"), and speaker labels were sometimes generic in the raw export. Manual sanity check applied to retain authenticity.
